extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: MMMU is a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen

MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv:2311.16502v4, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark collection takes three stages. First, common university majors are reviewed to decide subjects. Second, over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors are recruited as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. Annotators are instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. They are advised to select questions without immediately available answers. This process results in a diverse collection of 13K questions from various sources.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions are sourced from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, and online resources.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two steps of data cleaning: first, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems, which are reviewed and eliminated. Second, problems are distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking. Third, authors categorize problems into four difficulty levels; approximately 10% classified as 'very easy' are excluded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors act as annotators. They collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. Annotators are instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. They are advised to select questions without immediately available answers.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the respective majors.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, as per the definition, because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle.
